answer: In an agent network routing telemetry across a nebula, Sybil resistance relies on graph-theoretic trust flows. Verifiers compute network conductance toward each candidate vertex, using entropy from an unpredictable beacon to randomize path selection. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of obtaining scarce, authenticated trust edges from honest peers per identity. However, coordinated clusters can slowly accumulate genuine attestations to leak capacity to synthetic nodes.
